interactions.label: On bimanual palpation, which finding most reliably distinguishes a uterine fibro

params.question: On bimanual palpation, which finding most reliably distinguishes a uterine fibroid from an ovarian mass?

answers.text: The mass is non-tender on palpation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Non-tenderness is typical of fibroids but does not distinguish them from ovarian masses, many of which are also painless on palpation.

answers.text: The mass moves along with the cervix

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Because a fibroid arises from the uterine wall, it is continuous with the uterus. Moving the cervix during bimanual examination therefore transmits movement to the mass — a finding absent with an ovarian mass, which moves independently.

answers.text: The mass has an irregular surface

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: An irregular contour suggests fibroids but is not a reliable distinguishing feature. Ovarian masses such as dermoid cysts or endometriomas can also feel irregular.

answers.text: The mass is located above the pelvic brim

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Both large fibroids and large ovarian masses can extend above the pelvic brim, so suprapubic location alone does not differentiate the two.

overallFeedback.feedback: A fibroid moves with the cervix because it arises from the uterine wall and is continuous with the uterus. An ovarian mass, being a separate structure, moves independently of the cervix.
Correct — the fibroid is part of the uterine body, so cervical movement transmits directly to the mass. This is the key bimanual finding that separates it from an ovarian mass.

interactions.label: Which clinical feature best differentiates adenomyosis from endometriosis on exa

params.question: Which clinical feature best differentiates adenomyosis from endometriosis on examination?

answers.text: Presence of secondary dysmenorrhoea

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Both adenomyosis and endometriosis cause secondary dysmenorrhoea, so this symptom alone cannot differentiate the two conditions.

answers.text: A fixed, retroverted uterus with tender nodules in the posterior fornix

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: These findings are characteristic of endometriosis, not adenomyosis. They indicate adhesions and deposits involving the Pouch of Douglas and uterosacral ligaments.

answers.text: A uniformly enlarged, boggy, and tender uterus that remains mobile

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: In adenomyosis, endometrial tissue infiltrates the myometrium diffusely, producing symmetrical uterine enlargement with a soft, boggy feel. Unlike endometriosis, there are no pelvic adhesions, so uterine mobility is preserved.

answers.text: Deep dyspareunia with subfertility

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Deep dyspareunia and subfertility are hallmarks of endometriosis, particularly when disease involves the uterosacral ligaments and Pouch of Douglas.

overallFeedback.feedback: In adenomyosis the uterus is uniformly enlarged, boggy, and tender yet remains mobile. In endometriosis the uterus may be fixed by adhesions but is not enlarged. Pain dominates endometriosis; bleeding dominates adenomyosis.
Correct — the boggy, uniformly enlarged but mobile uterus is the hallmark of adenomyosis. In endometriosis the uterus may be fixed by adhesions but is not diffusely enlarged.

params.question: In uterine prolapse, symptoms of constipation and incomplete bowel evacuation result from descent of the anterior vaginal wall.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: These bowel symptoms result from a rectocele — descent of the posterior vaginal wall, not the anterior. Anterior wall descent (cystocele) causes urinary symptoms such as stress incontinence. Remember: anterior = bladder, posterior = bowel.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — constipation and incomplete evacuation arise from a rectocele, which is descent of the posterior vaginal wall. Anterior wall descent (cystocele) causes urinary symptoms such as stress incontinence and incomplete bladder emptying. A useful rule: anterior = bladder, posterior = bowel.

interactions.label: What is the most important reason hormone replacement therapy is recommended for

params.question: What is the most important reason hormone replacement therapy is recommended for women with premature ovarian insufficiency until the natural age of menopause?

answers.text: To restore regular menstrual cycles and ovulation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: HRT does not restore ovarian function or fertility. It replaces the hormones the ovaries are no longer producing, but ovulation does not resume.

answers.text: To reduce their elevated lifetime risk of osteoporosis and cardiovascular disease

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Early loss of ovarian oestrogen exposes these women to decades of hormone deficiency, substantially increasing their risk of fragility fractures and cardiovascular events compared to women who reach menopause at the usual age.

answers.text: To delay the onset of menopause until age fifty

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: HRT does not delay menopause. The ovaries have already ceased functioning; HRT simply provides exogenous hormones to mitigate the health consequences of their early loss.

answers.text: To prevent the development of endometrial carcinoma

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Unopposed oestrogen actually increases endometrial carcinoma risk. HRT for POI includes a progestogen to protect the endometrium, but cancer prevention is not the indication for prescribing it.

overallFeedback.feedback: Women with POI face decades of oestrogen deficiency, which substantially raises their lifetime risk of osteoporosis and cardiovascular disease. HRT until the natural menopause age (~50) replaces the missing hormones and mitigates this risk.

Correct — early cessation of ovarian oestrogen dramatically raises the lifetime risk of osteoporosis and cardiovascular disease. HRT until the natural menopause age (~50) replaces the missing hormones and reduces this excess risk.

interactions.label: A 60-year-old woman reports a single episode of light vaginal spotting, six year

params.question: A 60-year-old woman reports a single episode of light vaginal spotting, six years after her last menstrual period. She is not concerned because the bleeding was minimal. What is the most important reason this symptom requires urgent investigation?

answers.text: Light spotting in a postmenopausal woman always indicates cervical pathology

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Not all post-menopausal bleeding is cervical in origin. Endometrial, vaginal, and other pelvic pathologies can all present with minimal spotting. The key concern is endometrial pathology.

answers.text: Approximately 10% of women with post-menopausal bleeding have endometrial carcinoma, and bleeding amount does not predict pathology severity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A tiny spot could represent endometrial carcinoma, while heavy bleeding may come from a benign atrophic endometrium or a polyp. This dissociation between bleeding volume and pathology severity, combined with the 10% carcinoma prevalence, is why every case of PMB is investigated.

answers.text: Any vaginal bleeding after menopause is most likely due to endometrial carcinoma

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Carcinoma accounts for approximately 10% of PMB cases, not the majority. However, even this prevalence is high enough to mandate investigation of every single case without exception.

answers.text: Investigation is needed only if the spotting recurs within three months

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Even a single episode of PMB warrants urgent investigation. Delaying until recurrence risks missing a potentially curable endometrial carcinoma at an early, treatable stage.

overallFeedback.feedback: Approximately 10% of women with post-menopausal bleeding have endometrial carcinoma. Because the amount of bleeding does not correlate with the severity of the underlying cause, even a single episode of minimal spotting warrants urgent investigation.

Correct — the 10% prevalence of endometrial carcinoma and the poor correlation between bleeding amount and pathology severity together make every episode of PMB an absolute indication for urgent investigation.

interactions.label: A 33-year-old woman with a 7 cm intramural fibroid causing severe menorrhagia wi

params.question: A 33-year-old woman with a 7 cm intramural fibroid causing severe menorrhagia wishes to conceive in the future. Which management plan is most appropriate?

answers.text: Hysterectomy, as it offers a permanent cure with no risk of recurrence

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Hysterectomy is curative but removes the uterus entirely, making future pregnancy impossible. It is appropriate only for women who have completed their families.

answers.text: GnRH agonist therapy for three months followed by myomectomy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The GnRH agonist creates a temporary low-oestrogen state that shrinks the fibroid by 35–60%, reducing operative blood loss and surgical difficulty. Myomectomy then removes the fibroid while preserving the uterus for future conception.

answers.text: Levonorgestrel intrauterine system (Mirena) as definitive treatment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The LNG-IUS controls menstrual bleeding in women with smaller fibroids that do not distort the uterine cavity. It does not shrink large fibroids and is not suitable when conception is desired.

answers.text: Uterine artery embolisation to shrink the fibroid while preserving fertility

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: UAE reduces fibroid size by blocking its blood supply, but its safety in women planning pregnancy remains uncertain. It is generally reserved for women who are not planning future conception.

overallFeedback.feedback: For a woman who desires future pregnancy, myomectomy preserves the uterus while removing the fibroid. Pre-treatment with a GnRH agonist for three months shrinks the fibroid by 35–60% and reduces operative blood loss, making surgery safer and technically easier.
Correct — pre-treatment with a GnRH agonist followed by myomectomy is the standard approach for a large symptomatic fibroid in a woman who wishes to preserve her fertility.
